AP Business · Topic 2.1 · Marketing to customers

Token of Trust

How did Token of Trust choose its target customer—and was the decision justified?

4 people · 1 shared device 20–25 minutes after reading Explain. Evaluate. Justify.

Your conversation

Work is saved in this browser on this device. Use your teacher-provided case · College Board case resources

Run a better case conversation

For 28 students, use seven teams of four and one shared device per team. Students should read the four-page Token of Trust case first. This is an evaluation case: the founders’ B2B choice is known. Students explain how the evidence informed that choice and judge whether it was justified.

Before the conversation

Give two quiet minutes to distinguish the focus-group evidence from the price-premium evidence and identify an inference limit. Students then form an initial view of the B2B choice. Short notes and bilingual planning are welcome.

The structure is a Kagan-inspired adaptation of equal timed turns, paraphrase-before-response and individual accountability, rather than an official Kagan script.

During the conversation

Listen closely to two teams each round. Look for accurate case references, fair paraphrasing and a response to a different view.

Ask a student you select: “Explain a teammate’s reason, then tell me what you think.” Move beyond the most fluent volunteer.

Use the record as evidence

A completed field or a running timer does not establish understanding. Use the team record alongside your observation and brief individual follow-up.

Each student gives an independent exit response. Assess business meaning, evidence and listening; accent, speaking speed and confidence are not separate criteria.

Keep collection simple

Print or save one team record as a PDF. Collect it using your usual classroom process.

Names and writing stay in the browser on the current device. There is no live class dashboard or automatic submission. Export a backup before clearing the device.

Topic and skill connections

The discussion samples selected essential knowledge from all four Topic 2.1 objectives: 2.1.A, why and how marketers collect data; 2.1.B, using segmentation to identify a target customer; 2.1.C, customer relationships, acquisition cost and lifetime value; and 2.1.D, risks from collecting and using customer data.

3.C: compare B2C and B2B against stated criteria. 3.D: recommend whether to maintain or change a course of action, using evidence and a counterargument. 4.B: frame the final evaluation as a brief to business decision makers. 5.B/5.D: agree responsibilities and make useful contributions. One discussion samples these skills; it does not establish complete mastery.
